prompt: Stage 4-2, level 8, 51 gold, 57 HP. Your board is built around a 1-star Ahri holding two items. The shop shows a second Ahri. Buying her drops you to 47 gold, one interest tick below the cap, and you planned to roll at 4-5. Do you buy?

options.label: Buy the Ahri. A pair on your itemised carry is worth far more than 1 gold of interest
Skip it to stay at 50; you will find her again at 4-5
Buy her and roll to 30 right now for the third copy

explanation:
Interest is a 1-gold difference between 47 and 50 for one round: buying the pair costs you exactly 1 gold of income at 4-3. In return you hold 2 of the 10 Ahri copies in the pool, which turns the 4-5 rolldown from "find two copies" into "find one". At level 8 a shop has a 30% chance per slot of a 4-cost and there are fourteen 4-costs in this set, so a single Ahri appears in roughly 10% of slots. Needing one hit instead of two roughly halves the gold your rolldown will cost, which is worth far more than the 1 gold you gave up. You will also be back above 50 by 4-4 with the base income.

Rolling now is the wrong direction: 4-2 is not your planned rolldown, you are at 57 HP with two losses of slack, and rolling 20 gold at 4-2 leaves you with a weak rolldown at 4-5. The right shape is buy, hold, roll at the planned point with the pair already in hand.
principle: Breaking 50 by a few gold for a copy of your itemised carry is not greed; it is the cheapest roll you will ever get.
commonMistake: Treating the interest threshold as sacred and skipping a natural copy that a rolldown would later pay 10+ gold to find.
